reader.decision: Approve batching with 4 workers and a Retry-After retry (max 3). Implement it in sync/crm_client.py and sync/run_sync.py. Read the response shape from the first real response, and keep failed contacts unmarked.
reader.decision_reason: The message's numbers show backoff alone caps throughput at 100 contacts per minute, or 12,000 per run, against 46,800 contacts and a 2-hour deadline. Batching cuts the request count to 468 and removes the cause. The enterprise tier misses the 30 Oct deadline.

reconstruction.problem: The nightly sync sends one PUT per contact with 8 workers, which is about 400 requests per minute. Juniper allows 100 per minute per key. The Fairhaven import (TS-77) added 45,600 contacts, so 46,800 are pending.
reconstruction.what_breaks: About 300 requests per minute return 429, and those contacts stay unmarked until the next night. Throughput is capped at 100 contacts per minute, so the job needs 468 minutes against a 120-minute deadline. It hits activeDeadlineSeconds 7200 with 11,940 upserted and 34,860 pending, and sales misses the Friday 09:00 UTC deadline.
reconstruction.fix: Add upsert_batch(contacts) in sync/crm_client.py. It posts to /contacts:batchUpsert and retries up to 3 times on 429, sleeping for Retry-After. In sync/run_sync.py, sync_one becomes sync_batch, main chunks contacts into groups of 100, and WORKERS drops from 8 to 4. mark_synced runs only for per-contact successes. Delete upsert_contact once nothing calls it. This gives 468 calls in about 14 minutes.
reconstruction.cost: One code change in two files. Two risks: the batch response shape is not documented in docs/juniper-api.md, so it will be read from the first real response, and failed contacts within a batch must stay unmarked. The enterprise tier is not chosen. It costs 1,450 USD per month, has a 3-week lead time and misses the 30 Oct deadline.

reader.closing_answer: Yes, I approve batching with 4 workers and a Retry-After retry. Go ahead and implement it in sync/crm_client.py and sync/run_sync.py.
